entries.temporal: Late May–early June 1995, after Crouch disappearance
entries.model_notes: Observed operable window, lighting change and stored model. The later owl/mermaid dream images do not alter the physical classroom.

entries.description: Harry leaves through the Divination trapdoor and stepladder and walks the corridors to the stone gargoyle guarding Dumbledore’s entrance.
entries.temporal: Late May–early June 1995, after Crouch disappearance
entries.model_notes: No traced floor-by-floor descent is supplied.

entries.location: Headmaster’s moving staircase and outer door
entries.description: After failed password guesses, Cockroach cluster makes the gargoyle jump aside. Harry enters a gap in the wall and stands on a spiral stone stair which slowly carries him upwards as the lower doors close, reaching a polished oak door with a brass knocker. Office voices can be heard beyond it.
entries.temporal: Late May–early June 1995, after Crouch disappearance
entries.model_notes: Dated valid password. Preserve the moving stair and separate upper office door; no numeric rise or fixed floor count is given.

entries.description: The office is a beautiful circular room lined with sleeping portraits of previous headmasters and headmistresses. Dumbledore has a polished desk and chair with a visitor chair opposite and enough space to pace behind it. Fawkes occupies a golden perch beside the door; the office is sunlit.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1995 office visit; earlier school memory where specified
entries.model_notes: Clunks can be heard fading in the corridor below after visitors depart. No measured diameter is supplied.

entries.description: Behind Dumbledore’s desk a shelf holds the ragged Sorting Hat. Beside it a glass case displays Gryffindor’s silver sword with large rubies in its hilt.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1995 office visit; earlier school memory where specified
entries.model_notes: The sword’s history is given by narration; preserve the current glass case and shelf positions.

entries.description: A black cabinet behind the visitor chair contains a shallow stone basin carved with runes and symbols, filled with moving silver-white memory substance. Its light reflects on the sword case. Touching the surface draws Harry into a memory; Dumbledore retrieves him and moves the basin onto the polished desk, where stored memories can also project revolving figures.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1995 office visit; earlier school memory where specified
entries.model_notes: Magical memory access is not a physical tunnel or extra room beneath the cabinet. The courtroom shown in the basin is outside Hogwarts.

entries.description: The narration compares the memory courtroom’s bracket-mounted wall torches to those illuminating Hogwarts walls.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1995 office visit; earlier school memory where specified
entries.model_notes: Only the stated Hogwarts fixture comparison is imported; the courtroom’s square plan, benches and chained chairs do not belong to the castle.

entries.location: Space behind greenhouses in school memory
entries.description: A projected memory of school-age Bertha Jorkins reports that she saw a pupil kissing Florence behind the greenhouses.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1995 office visit; earlier school memory where specified
entries.model_notes: Reported historical use of space behind the greenhouses; the memory does not show its planting, geometry or exact year.

entries.description: McGonagall permits lunchtime use of the empty Transfiguration classroom. Its window looks down onto a tree under which Malfoy, Crabbe and Goyle stand, and there is an open central practice area.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: Specific window sightline; no bearing or whole-ground panorama is stated.

entries.description: Violet occupies a frame in the chamber off the Great Hall and winks at Bill. Bill asks after the portrait of the mad knight Sir Cadogan, and Harry confirms it remains in the school.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: Violet’s chamber location is observed. Cadogan’s present existence is reported without a frame location.

entries.location: Fat Lady in earlier school years
entries.description: Mrs Weasley remembers the Fat Lady guarding the dormitory entrance during her school years, including a reprimand after a four-a.m. return from a walk.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: Reported earlier use of the same guardian; no exact year is given.

entries.description: During a sunny tour of the carriage, ship and grounds, Mrs Weasley is intrigued by the Whomping Willow, which was planted after her school years. The group can also walk around the greenhouses.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: Relative planting date only; no date or tree position should be invented.

entries.description: Bagman and Fudge join the staff table, Fudge next to Maxime, as the enchanted ceiling shifts from blue to dusky purple before departure for the task.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: Dated seating and light transition.

entries.location: Third-task maze exterior and safety patrol
entries.description: The Quidditch pitch is enclosed by a twenty-foot hedge with an entrance gap facing the arriving champions and a dark path beyond. Spectators occupy the stands. Four staff patrol outside the maze in separate directions, marked by luminous red stars, and explain that red sparks signal a rescue.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: The previously planned twenty-foot height is now observed. Rescue by sparks is an announced rule; the stands’ exact view into the maze is not established.

entries.location: Maze entry acoustics and first fork
entries.description: High thick hedges shadow the path and silence the outside crowd immediately on entry, though subsequent starting whistles can be heard. Harry and Cedric reach a fork about fifty yards in; Harry takes left, Cedric right, and Harry then turns right. The maze darkens as the sky becomes navy.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: The cause of crowd suppression may be hedge density or enchantment; narrator leaves it uncertain. Fifty yards measures entry to first fork only.

entries.location: Maze north-west course and rejoining paths
entries.description: At a second fork Harry’s Four-Point Spell indicates north through the hedge to his right. He needs north-west for the centre, takes left and then an available right. Cedric emerges from a path on the right and departs down another path. Later Harry encounters left/right turns and dead ends, checks that he has strayed east, and backtracks.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: A compass constraint and ordered local route, not enough for a unique full maze plan. Cedric reports enormous Skrewts on his route.

entries.description: Around a corner a twelve-foot Dementor shape approaches Harry, producing cold and rattling breathing. A Patronus drives it back and it stumbles, exposing a Boggart; Riddikulus dispels it as smoke.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: A tournament obstacle with transformed appearance, not a real Dementor permanently stationed in the grounds.

entries.description: Golden mist blocks a path, unaffected by Reducto. Running through it makes Harry experience ground overhead and starry sky beneath him while his feet seem stuck to the grass. Pulling one foot free restores normal orientation and he emerges from the mist to a junction, taking right.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: Observed disorientation enchantment; the text does not prove the whole world literally inverted. A scream from ahead is audible through the maze.

entries.description: After ten minutes of dead ends and a repeated wrong turn, Harry rounds a corner into a ten-foot armoured Skrewt. Spells rebound from its armour until Impedimenta hits its soft underside. Harry escapes, finds more left/right dead ends, backtracks and selects a north-westward path.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: Creature size and spell interaction govern local clearance and hazard design; its frozen state is temporary.

entries.description: Harry hears Cedric and Krum in a parallel path but cannot find a connecting route. Reducto burns a small hole in the hedge; he kicks through thick brambles and branches, tears his robes passing through, and sees them to his right. After Krum is Stunned face-down in the grass, Cedric shoots red rescue sparks above him; the two continue and split left/right.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: A damaged local hedge connection, with audible voices across the barrier. Do not model all hedges as indestructible or all adjacent paths as connected.

entries.description: Past further dead ends a sphinx blocks a long straight path near the goal. It paces side to side, then sits in the middle and states that the quickest route passes it; a correct first riddle answer permits passage, a wrong answer provokes attack, and silence permits retreat. It moves aside when Harry answers spider.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: Creature checkpoint and conditional access; no permanent stone gateway is described.

entries.location: Maze Cup approach and spider damage
entries.description: At a later fork Harry follows the wand-guided right-hand path and sees the gleaming Cup on a plinth a hundred yards ahead. Cedric joins from another route. A gigantic spider visible over the left hedge advances along an intersecting path; it lifts and drops Harry twelve feet, then combined Stunning Spells topple it sideways, flattening a hedge and filling the path with tangled legs. The Cup is only feet from Cedric after the fight.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: Preserve local crossing, final straight view, plinth and temporary hedge damage. The twelve-foot fall is not a measured spider height.

entries.description: When Harry and Cedric grasp the Cup’s handles together at its plinth, both are pulled off the ground and transported while unable to release it.
entries.temporal: June 1995 preparation and 24 June third task; history where stated
entries.model_notes: Observed Portkey effect inside Hogwarts grounds. This is distinct from Apparition restrictions and does not establish that all Portkeys are blocked or enabled.

entries.description: After the Cup transports them away, Harry notes that even the mountains surrounding Hogwarts are no longer present.
entries.model_notes: Establishes a mountainous castle setting through a narrated contrast. The guessed tens or hundreds of miles travelled are not a measured separation.

entries.description: Voldemort says his agent at Hogwarts converted the Cup into a Portkey so that the first champion touching it would be transported beyond Dumbledore’s protection.
entries.model_notes: A reported hostile modification, distinct from an ordinary route to the school. Other protective statements here are general and do not establish new castle walls or wards.

entries.description: James’s echo tells Harry the Cup will return him to Hogwarts. Harry summons it while holding Cedric’s body, grasps its handle, and the Portkey transports both away together.
entries.model_notes: Observed reuse and transport of a person/body in contact with the holder. Arrival location is supplied by the next chapter; the remote graveyard itself is outside the model scope.

entries.description: The returning Cup deposits Harry and Cedric’s body on grass at the edge of the maze, below the spectator stands and open starry sky, where the crowd can close in around them.
entries.temporal: 24 June 1995 return and interrogation; prior-year events where reported
entries.model_notes: The return target is the maze edge, rather than necessarily the central plinth from which they departed.

entries.description: The impostor takes Harry across the lawn past the lake and ship, up the castle stone steps, through the Entrance Hall, up the marble staircase and along a corridor into Moody’s office.
entries.temporal: 24 June 1995 return and interrogation; prior-year events where reported
entries.model_notes: A contiguous sequence without an exact floor number. The destination is concealed from Harry under the claim of hospital care.

entries.location: Moody’s office confinement and damaged door
entries.description: The dark office has a keyed lock and a barred door; screams from the distant Quidditch pitch remain audible. Dumbledore blasts the door apart with a Stunning Spell, splintering it and leaving a breached doorway.
entries.temporal: 24 June 1995 return and interrogation; prior-year events where reported
entries.model_notes: Dated damage. The magical eye is used to check the space outside the closed door; ordinary Harry has no equivalent sightline.

entries.description: Three indistinct figures in the wall-mounted Foe-Glass sharpen as Dumbledore, Snape and McGonagall approach; their faces remain visible in it after they stand in the doorway and enter. Crouch is later seated against the wall beneath it.
entries.temporal: 24 June 1995 return and interrogation; prior-year events where reported
entries.model_notes: Observed display behaviour corroborates its warning function; it is not an ordinary mirror of the room.

entries.description: Each keyhole opens a different interior of the same trunk: first spellbooks, then broken Sneakoscopes, parchment, quills and a silvery Invisibility Cloak, with other unspecified contents in compartments three to six. The seventh reveals a pit-like room ten feet below containing the real Moody. Dumbledore climbs down, covers him against the cold and climbs back out.
entries.temporal: 24 June 1995 return and interrogation; prior-year events where reported
entries.model_notes: Nested magical interior, not proof of a cellar excavated beneath the office. No ladder is described; the ten-foot drop is explicit.

entries.description: Crouch reports summoning Dobby to the staff room to collect robes for cleaning, then staging a loud conversation about Gillyweed and the hostages to direct him towards Snape’s store cupboard.
entries.temporal: 24 June 1995 return and interrogation; prior-year events where reported
entries.model_notes: Reported manipulation under the Moody disguise. This resolves the overheard-conversation provenance without changing staff-room geometry.

entries.description: Crouch says his borrowed magical eye let him see through the outer maze hedges while patrolling and remove obstacles with curses. He says he Stunned Fleur and placed Krum under Imperius to attack Cedric.
entries.temporal: 24 June 1995 return and interrogation; prior-year events where reported
entries.model_notes: Reported hostile intervention explains an unusually clear route; do not generalise Harry’s low obstacle count to the intended maze population.

entries.location: Real Moody’s confinement and ingredient theft
entries.description: Crouch reports bringing the captured real Moody, clothes and detectors to Hogwarts in Moody’s own magical trunk, keeping him alive under Imperius for hair and interrogation, and stealing Polyjuice ingredients from Snape’s dungeon stores. The map’s Bartemius Crouch label referred to the son with the same name.
entries.temporal: 24 June 1995 return and interrogation; prior-year events where reported
entries.model_notes: Narrated discovery confirms the prisoner; the yearlong treatment and thefts are a confession. Earlier references to Moody as teacher concern this impostor.

entries.location: Forest ambush and Hagrid excavation burial
entries.description: Crouch says he entered the grounds under an Invisibility Cloak, ambushed Krum and killed his father at the Forest edge, carried the body deeper among the trees, doubled behind Harry and Dumbledore, and later Transfigured the body into a bone and buried it in the fresh earth in front of Hagrid’s cabin.
entries.temporal: 24 June 1995 return and interrogation; prior-year events where reported
entries.model_notes: Reported hidden sequence and temporary burial state, correcting the earlier unexplained disappearance. The confession gives no grave depth or exact point within the excavation.

entries.description: Crouch reports volunteering to carry the Cup into the maze before dinner and converting it into the Portkey.
entries.temporal: 24 June 1995 return and interrogation; prior-year events where reported
entries.model_notes: Reported timing and means of illicit route creation; supports the observed transport and Voldemort’s account.

entries.description: Dumbledore takes Harry from Moody’s office along a dark passage to the gargoyle, then up the moving spiral stair and through the oak door into his office.
entries.model_notes: The destination is described as up; no intervening floor count is given.

entries.description: Harry, Dumbledore and Sirius leave the office and descend a flight of stairs to the hospital-wing entrance.
entries.model_notes: Preserve the stated descent; do not assume this single mentioned flight accounts for every intermediate threshold.

entries.description: The hospital wing has a long ward with beds extending to a far end, bedside tables or cabinets, visitor chairs on either side of a bed, portable privacy screens, lamps, windows, pillows and feather mattresses. Pomfrey has her own office from which she brings potions. Harry’s bed is nearer the entrance than the real Moody’s bed at the far end.
entries.model_notes: Dated patients and bedside medical objects need not remain permanently. The ward door has a handle Sirius can operate with a paw, but no height measurement is given.

entries.description: Snape and McGonagall report that Fudge brought a Dementor into the castle and up to the office despite Dumbledore’s policy against them; it immediately attacked the bound Crouch there.
entries.model_notes: Reported incident proves the policy was not an automatically impassable physical or magical boundary. It adds no reported building damage.

entries.description: Two bucket-sized cups and saucers stand on the table before the fireplace, and Hagrid takes additional cups from the dresser for visitors.
entries.model_notes: Adds oversized household ware and dresser storage, without changing the single-room plan.

entries.description: For the Leaving Feast the usual winning-house decorations are absent. Black mourning drapes hang behind the staff table. Maxime sits beside Hagrid, Snape beside McGonagall, and Karkaroff’s chair is empty. Pupils rise from benches to toast Cedric.
entries.model_notes: Dated mourning layout and seating; confirms benches at the house tables.

entries.description: Pupils wait with luggage in the Entrance Hall for carriages to Hogsmeade station. The apparently horseless vehicles trundle up the drive to collect them.
entries.model_notes: Return leg of the ordinary station route. The station journey itself is not narrated in detail.

entries.description: From the castle entrance Harry sees Hagrid harnessing the giant horses far across the grounds as the carriage prepares to take off; Fleur walks back across the lawns to it.
entries.model_notes: A long entrance-to-carriage sightline and departure state. Do not infer that the carriage has already flown away in this paragraph.

entries.description: Krum says Karkaroff stayed in his cabin while the students operated the ship.
entries.model_notes: Reported cabin existence and ship operation; the departing voyage is not shown.

entries.description: Hermione says she caught Rita’s beetle form on a hospital-wing sill and identifies her as an unregistered Animagus. Harry recalls the beetle on the stone reindeer; Hermione links it to the lakeside conversation, Malfoy’s hand beneath the tree and probably the Divination window-sill.
entries.model_notes: The captive beetle and markings are observed, but its earlier spying locations are recollections or deductions. The Divination perch remains explicitly tentative. A human visitor ban does not prevent a beetle reaching these points.

entries.location: Hogsmeade to London return rail route
entries.description: The Hogwarts Express carries pupils south in clear summer weather and arrives at King’s Cross platform nine and three-quarters, where Harry leaves through the barrier to meet his uncle.
entries.model_notes: Completes regional school-access context. Train compartments have sliding doors; their later confrontation causes no stated permanent carriage damage.
